Manoj Kumar vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 31 March,
2026
 Neutral Citation No. 2026:Mphc-Gwl:10588
 1 
 In The High Court Of Madhya Pradesh
At Gwalior

Before
 Hon'Ble Shri Justice Rajesh Kumar Gupta

On The 31st Of March, 2026
 Misc. Criminal Case No. 11214 of 2026
 Manoj Kumar
 Versus
 The State Of Madhya Pradesh
 Appearance:
 Mr. Rudra Pratap Singh Kaurav - Advocate for the appl
 Mr. Rajeev Shrivastava - Special Prosecutor for the r
 Order

This is the first application under Section 482 of the Bhartiya Nagrik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 for grant of anticipatory bail filed by the applicant in connection with Crime No.95 of 2025 registered at Police Station E.O.W., District Gwalior (M.P.) for the offence under Sections 420, 409, 120-B of IPC and Section 7, 13(1) and 12(2) of Prevention of Corruption Act.
2. The allegation against the applicant is that, while serving as a Sub- Registrar posted at Lahar, he executed six registered sale deeds on various dates.

Although the stamp duty and registration fees should have been paid according to the Collector's guidelines, a lower amount was paid, resulting in a total revenue loss of Rs. 8,45,309/- to the Government.
Consequently, the aforementioned offence was registered against the applicant.
3. The applicant apprehends arrest in connection with the aforesaid crime.
It is further submitted t h a t t h e a p p l i c a n t i s a G o v e r n m e n t S e r v a n t a n d N E U T R A L C I T A T I O N N O .
2026:MPHC-GWL:10588 2 MCRC-11214-2026 there is no possibility of his absconding in the matter.
He is ready to abide by all the terms and conditions that may be imposed.

It is further prayed that appropriate directions be issued to the Investigating Officer/Trial Court to strictly adhere to the mandate laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Arnesh Kumar vs. State of Bihar,
(2014) 8 SCC 273 .

It is further submitted that co-accused Rohit Saxena (M.Cr.C.
No. 29861 of 2025) and Seema Kushwah (M.Cr.C. No. 28227 of 2025) have already been granted Manoj Kumar vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 31 March, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/8468347/
1 bail by a Coordinate Bench of this Court.

sentences.text: On these grounds, it is prayed that the application for grant of anticipatory bail may be considered.
4. On the other hand, learned counsel for the respondent/EOW opposes the bail application and submits that the applicant's interrogation is necessary as the matter is still under investigation

;
therefore, at this stage, the applicant is not entitled to the grant of anticipatory bail.

It is further submitted that the applicant, being a Government Officer, executed six registered sale deeds where the stamp duty and registration fees were paid at a lower rate than required by the Collector's guidelines, resulting in a total revenue loss of Rs.8,45,309/- to the Government.
In such circumstances, counsel prayed for the dismissal of the present bail application.

5. Heard, counsel for the parties and perused the record.
6.

From a perusal of the record, it is seen that although the applicant is NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2026:MPHC-GWL:10588 3 MCRC-11214-2026 a Government servant, the allegations against him are serious in nature.

Prima facie, certain forgeries were committed by the applicant in the execution of registered sale deeds, whereby stamp duty and registration fees were paid at a lower rate than required by the Collector's guidelines.

This resulted in a total revenue loss of Rs.
8,45,309/- to the Government.
Considering the gravity of the allegations, as well as the fact that the investigation is still ongoing, this Court is not inclined to grant anticipatory bail to the applicant at this stage.
7. Accordingly, present anticipatory application is hereby dismissed.

(RAJESH KUMAR GUPTA ) JUDGE (LJ*)
